 Nidhi Gupta, J.
Cm-12600-Cii-2021 Prayer in this application filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act is for
condonation of delay of 443 days in filing the accompanying appeal.

2.  The only reason cited by learned counsel for the applicant/appellant in the abovesaid application for condonation of 443 days delay in filing the appeal is as under:-
"2.

That delay has been accrued because the appellant filed application under section 153 read with section 115 of Code of Civil Procedure on 11.02.2020 for correction of his name as Mannat Bajaj in place of Manant Bajaj in the award dated 02.11.2019.
3.

That the above mentioned application allowed on 07.01.2021 and the counsel for the appellant applied for certified copy of order dated 07.01.2021 on 08.01.2021 and the same was prepared on 19.01.2021 and the counsel received the same on FAO-3030-2021 (O&M) - 2- 21.01.2021.
The certified copy of order dated 07.01.2021 is attached as Annexure A-1."

3. However, it is to be noted that no proof whatsoever has been produced by the applicant/appellant to substantiate his contention that any application had been filed by the appellant for correction of his name in the Award dated 02.11.2019.
Even the order dated 07.01.2021 has not been appended alongwith the present appeal.
In fact, in the Award appended by the applicant alongwith present appeal, name of the appellant is mentioned as 'Manant Bajaj.'
Thus, there is nothing on record to indicate that the order dated 7.1.2021 was passed whereby name of the applicant was changed.

5. As such, no ground is made out for condoning inordinate delay of 443 days.
Present application accordingly stands dismissed.

The present appeal has been filed by the injured-claimant seeking enhancement of compensation of Rs.3,38,100/- awarded by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jalandhar (for short "the learned Tribunal") vide Award dated 02.11.2019 passed in MACP Case No. 166 dated 17.07.2018 filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

2. Brief facts of the case are that the ld. Tribunal on the basis of evidence adduced by the parties concluded that the appellant had suffered injuries in a motor vehicular accident that took place on 26.01.2018 due to the rash and negligent driving of Innova Car bearing registration No. PIQ- 0062 (hereinafter "the offending vehicle") being driven by respondent No.1; owned by respondent No.2;
and insured by respondent No.3.

The abovesaid compensation was awarded along with interest @
7.5% per annum.
All the respondents were held jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant seeks enhancement of compensation by submitting that learned Tribunal has failed to grant loss of income, and transportation to the appellant.
Even less amount has been awarded for special diet and attendant charges.
Due to injuries suffered by the appellant in the accident in question, appellant has lost chance to join Army and other forces like Police.
Nothing has been awarded on account of loss of marriage prospects.
It is accordingly prayed that the present Appeal be allowed; and the compensation be enhanced.
4. Notice of motion.

sentences.text: Mr. D.K.Prajapati, Advocate accepts notice on behalf of respondent No.3-Insurance Company and submits that mediation was going FAO-3030-2021 (O&M) - 4- on between the appellant and respondent No.3-Insurance Company in which Insurance Company has assigned the case to him.

6. Learned counsel for respondent No.3 opposes submissions made on behalf of the appellant and submits that the impugned Award suffers from no infirmity as the compensation awarded to the appellant is just and fair.
Hence, the present appeal deserves to be dismissed.
7. No other argument is raised on behalf of the parties.
I have heard learned counsel and perused the case file in detail.
I find no merit in the submissions advanced on behalf of the appellant.

8. Perusal of the record of the case shows that it was the pleaded case of the appellant before the Tribunal that in the accident in question, appellant had suffered "multiple grievous injuries as a result of which he had remained under treatment at Patel Hospital, Jalandhar, from 26.01.2018 to 30.01.2018."
Appellant had further alleged that he had suffered defacement/disfigurement due to which his future prospects of service, marriage, social contacts had been adversely affected and are bleak.
It was further pleaded that the appellant "May have to take plastic surgery or skin grafting surgeries in future involving high expenditures".

Accordingly, compensation of Rs.43,90,949/-
alongwith interest was prayed for.

9. Learned Tribunal had concluded that the disfigurement of the face of the appellant was apparent from the photographs Mark PW1/C to Mark PW1/E; as also proved when the appellant had appeared in person in Court.

Furthermore, appellant had examined PW3 Dr. Baldev Raj Virdi, who had deposed that after examining the appellant, he had treated him vide FAO-3030-2021 (O&M) -
5- certificate Ex.PW1/34.
He further deposed that total estimate cost of future treatment of appellant would be Rs.2,08,000/-.
Appellant had proved medical bills/receipts Ex.PW1/1 to Ex.PW1/33 for a total amount of Rs.1,17,570/-.
Admittedly, appellant had not been able to prove that he had suffered any permanent functional disability in the accident in question.
Appellant had also not produced any proof of his income.
Thus, learned Tribunal had awarded the compensation in the following manner:-
Sr . Heads

Amount  No.
 1.

Medical bills and future Rs.3,25,570/-
 treatment expenses  2. Mental agony and physical pain Rs.5,000/-
 3. Special diet Rs.5,000/-
4 . Attendant charges Rs.2,500/-
From the above facts, it is clear that a more than just and fair compensation has been awarded to the appellants.

sentences.text: The expression, 'just' means that the amount so determined is fair, reasonable and equitable by accepted legal standards and not a forensic lottery -

Obviously 'just compensation' does not mean 'perfect' or 'absolute' compensation - The just compensation principle requires examination of the particular situation obtaining uniquely in an individual case."
12. Keeping in view the entirety of the above noted facts, the present Appeal is hereby dismissed on merits, as well as on ground of delay.
